questiontext.text:
A student wonders whether {@lhsA = rhsA@} for every real number \(x\). They check \(x = {@ra@}\), \(x = {@rb@}\) and \(x = {@rc@}\), and find that the two sides are equal each time.

(a) Complete one of the checks: when \(x = {@rb@}\), both sides equal

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) The student concludes that the equation is true for every real number \(x\). Show that the student is wrong: give an example of a value of \(x\) for which the two sides are different.

\(x =\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Type fractions as 1/2 and square roots as sqrt(2).

generalfeedback.text:
Checking values can show that a statement is false, but no number of checks can show that it is true for every real number: there are always values you have not checked.

(a) When \(x = {@rb@}\), the left-hand side is \({@rb@}^3 + {@s2@} \times {@rb@} = {@tval@}\) and the right-hand side is \({@s1@} \times {@rb@}^2 + {@s3@} = {@tval@}\).

(b) Subtracting the right-hand side from the left-hand side gives

\[\left({@lhsA@}\right) - \left({@rhsA@}\right) = (x - {@ra@})(x - {@rb@})(x - {@rc@}).\]

This product is 0 exactly when \(x\) is {@ra@}, {@rb@} or {@rc@}, the three values the student happened to check, and it is not 0 for any other value of \(x\). So any other value is a counterexample. For example, at \(x = 0\) the left-hand side is 0 and the right-hand side is {@s3@}.

questionnote.text: Claim {@lhsA = rhsA@}, true only at x = {@ra@}, {@rb@}, {@rc@}; check value {@tval@}

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the discussion of checking the proposition x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1) by substituting values of x (p. 5) in Section 2 of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022.

feedbackvariables.text: /* No diagnostic: a single substitution, so any wrong value is an arithmetic slip. */

falsefeedback.text: Substitute \(x = {@rb@}\) into each side. The left-hand side is \({@rb@}^3 + {@s2@} \times {@rb@}\).

node.description: The two sides differ at the student's value

truefeedback.text: At \(x = {@sx@}\) the left-hand side is [[if test="Lrat"]]{@Lv@}[[else]]about {@dispdp(float(Lv), 2)@}[[/if]] and the right-hand side is [[if test="Rrat"]]{@Rv@}[[else]]about {@dispdp(float(Rv), 2)@}[[/if]]. They are different, so the equation is not true for every real number \(x\). One value where it fails is enough to show this.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="Lrat"]]At \(x = {@sx@}\) both sides equal {@Lv@}, so this value agrees with the claim: it is one of the values the student checked.[[else]]At \(x = {@sx@}\) the two sides are equal, so this value agrees with the claim: it is equal to one of the values the student checked.[[/if]] Choose a value of \(x\) that the student did not check.
